Article Title: 'Agitation does not mean lathicharge': SC on police action against students protesting paper leak
Article Text:
CJI said the Constitution guarantees the right to peaceful protest.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday said the right to peaceful protest is constitutionally guaranteed and that the mere existence of an agitation cannot justify alleged police excesses against demonstrators.A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant made the observations while hearing pleas alleging police excesses against students during the July 20 protests over the NEET paper leak.The bench also indicated that a uniform nationwide protocol was needed to facilitate peaceful protests while enabling authorities to act against anti-social elements."Right to peaceful protests is in the Constitution. Right to peaceful protest is absolutely guaranteed. That cannot be denied. Merely because there is agitation cannot justify police excess," the CJI observed.Emphasising the need to protect both protesters and law enforcement personnel, the bench said, "Agitation does not mean lathicharge. Also, agitation does not mean violence."The court said pan-India guidelines should be framed on the issue without either the petitioners or governments adopting an adversarial approach.The bench, however, also expressed concern over allegations of attacks on police personnel during protests.When a lawyer referred to injuries suffered by police personnel and alleged attacks on their families by an unruly mob, Justice Joymalya Bagchi said, "Injury to police is of equal concern. We may call upon the State to respond why adequate safeguards were not provided…"The CJI said there should be a clear protocol governing peaceful protests across the country, including the provision of designated spaces for demonstrations."There should be a protocol when someone wants to agitate peacefully. Proper space for that. There is no impediment in that regard. But if there is any anti-social element that can be dealt with," the CJI said.The court observed that the matter required an all-India approach and indicated that mandatory guidelines could be evolved to ensure uniformity."It’s a question of all India… this uniformity in protocol is also… Self-discipline is integral to the entire process," the CJI observed.The matter has been listed for further hearing on Tuesday.
Article Summary: Cji said the constitution guarantees the right to peaceful protest. A bench led by chief justice of india surya kant made the observations while hearing pleas alleging police excesses against students during the neet paper leak. The court said pan-india guidelines should be framed on the issue.

Article Title: 'Indian students made us all proud': Greta Thunberg joins London protest in solidarity
Article Text:
Greta Thunberg stands in solidarity with CJP-led student protest (Image: X@/epppyyy)

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the top priority to prevent exam irregularities? Stronger security measures Better monitoring and transparency 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Climate activist Greta Thunberg on Sunday expressed support for the CJP-led student protest over irregularities in the education system, saying their movement demonstrated "the true meaning of people power. "Speaking at a gathering organised by the Students' Federation of India (SFI) in London, Thunberg said the students' fight for justice and the broader struggle for democracy and liberation was a shared cause that required international solidarity."The Indian Student Protest, has made us all proud! They have given us hope! They show what we can accomplish when people come together and resist. They show the true meaning of people power. The Indian student's struggle for justice and the broader struggle for democracy and liberation is also our struggle. So we all have to come together now and rise up in solidarity with India," said Greta Thunberg. She was attending a gathering organised by SFI in London," she said while addressing the gathering.The Students' Federation of India (SFI) UK organised the weekend gathering, describing it as a celebration of the movement's victory.“SFI UK salutes the struggle of the student movement and its success in pushing the education minister to resign,” SFI UK said in a statement.“The fight has been very inspiring and courageous. But it has certainly not yet come to an end. We continue to grieve for the 21 students who have lost their lives due to the handling of NEET, and of course, the brutal police repression against protestors,” it stated.The developments come after the 36-day agitation led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) culminated in the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister.The protest, which began on June 20, gathered momentum after police action against demonstrators on July 20 and went on to receive backing from several student organisations and activists, including Sonam Wangchuk, who undertook a prolonged hunger strike in solidarity with the movement.The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) announced on Saturday that it was calling off the 36-day agitation after the Centre agreed to its remaining demands, including compensation for the families of students who allegedly died by suicide following the NEET paper leak and the withdrawal of FIRs registered against protesters.Calling the past 36 days "really, really difficult", CJP leader Dipke thanked supporters across the country for backing the fledgling outfit despite widespread scepticism about its campaign.
Article Summary: Greta thunberg stands in solidarity with cjp-led student protest. She said the students' fight for justice and the broader struggle for democracy and liberation was a shared cause that required international solidarity. The cockroach janta party (cjp) announced on saturday that it was calling off the 36-day agitation.

Article Title: Dharmendra Pradhan resigns as Union education minister amid massive student protests
Article Text:
Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the most critical factor in shaping India's education system? Inclusivity Quality of education Access to resources Student feedback 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan on Saturday tendered his resignation from the Council of Ministers amid the ongoing protests over the NEET paper leak.In a letter addressed to his "young friends," Pradhan said that he has sent his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi , considering the situation that has developed at Jantar Mantar and across the country."I have been dedicated to students, teachers, and education reform for more than four decades. I have always believed that a strong, inclusive, and visionary education system is the very foundation of a strong nation. I deeply respect the aspirations, emotions, and just expectations of the country's youth. Realizing the dreams of India's young generation has been a moral commitment of all of us in political and social life.I express my gratitude to the Hon'ble Prime Minister for the opportunity he gave me to serve the nation under his visionary leadership," Pradhan said."Considering the situation that has developed at Jantar Mantar and across the country — that anti-national forces should not take advantage of this situation, that the unity of the country should be preserved, that not even a single student's future should get entangled in legal complications, and that our children should devote their time to studies and focus on building their careers — I have sent my resignation to the Hon'ble Prime Minister," he added.Also Read | Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation letter Pradhan said that the government took immediate cognizance when irregularities in the NEET-UG examination came to light."However, irregularities came to light in the NEET-UG examination held on 3 May 2026. The Government of India took immediate cognizance of this, handed over the investigation to the CBI, cancelled the examination, and announced a new date for the re-examination. Alongside this, it was decided that from next year the examination would be conducted in CBT (Computer-Based Test) mode," he added.In his letter, Pradhan also accused "certain individuals" of misleading students.Also Read | 'We won't go': CJP's Dipke says protests to continue till all demands met "From the very first day, I took responsibility and never turned away from this situation. My resolve was that we would not let any meritorious student's chances be ruined because of an examination mafia, and that no injustice would be done to any student. The NEET-UG results declared on 16 July were satisfactory, with many meritorious students from poor backgrounds also achieving success," he said."However, during this time too, certain individuals occupying positions of responsibility tried to mislead students and create obstruction, which caused me deep anguish. I have always been an unwavering believer in the strength of our democracy, and I have always held deep respect for the aspirations, dreams, and expectations of the youth. They are not only India's future, but also the bearers, builders, and architects of a new and developed India," he added."Watching the events of the last 10 days has saddened me. This is not a matter of personal reputation for me. The youth power of India is the real strength of this country. My resolve is that we will not let the country's youth get caught in a web of confusion," he further said.
Article Summary: Union education minister dharmendra pradhan tendered his resignation from the council of ministers on saturday. His resignation comes amid the ongoing protests over the neet paper leak. In a letter addressed to his "young friends," prdhan said that he has sent his resignation to prime minister narendra modi.

Article Title: PM Modi returns with message to students, announces Nandan Nilekani-led task force on exam reforms
Article Text:
Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support the formation of a task force to reform Indian examination system? Yes, it's necessary No, it won't make a difference 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday announced the constitution of a high-powered task force headed by technology expert Nandan Nilekani to recommend reforms aimed at making India's examination system more reliable, transparent and technology-driven.In a video message addressed to students, the PM Modi said the government had already taken several steps to safeguard the future of students, including action against those involved in examination malpractice, the establishment of fast-track courts and the introduction of tougher legal provisions through new legislation."The Government of India is continuously taking various measures for the future of students.Those who tampered with the students' future are languishing in jail. We have already established fast-track courts. We are also moving towards enacting new legislation in Parliament that incorporates stringent legal provisions. However, we must look to the future. Our examination system needs to be reliable and transparent, and it must make maximum use of technology. Keeping all these factors in mind, we have decided to constitute a high-powered task force under the leadership of the world-renowned technology expert Nandan Nilekani.This task force will focus on examination reforms, and based on its report, steps will be taken to ensure the credibility of upcoming examinations at the earliest," PM Modi said.The announcement comes amid the Centre's push to strengthen the examination process following recent controversies over irregularities in competitive examinations. The government has also proposed amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, providing for time-bound investigations, fast-track trials and enhanced penalties for paper leaks and organised examination fraud.The Nandan Nilekani-led task force is expected to examine the use of technology and recommend systemic reforms to improve transparency, credibility and efficiency in the conduct of public examinations across the country.
Article Summary: Prime minister narendra modi announces constitution of high-powered task force. Nandan nilekani-led task force to recommend reforms aimed at making india's examination system more reliable, transparent and technology-driven. Announcement comes amid centre's push to strengthen the examination process following recent controversies.

Article Title: At no point did government stop students from protesting: Nirmala Sitharaman
Article Text:
File photo: Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

NEW DELHI: Government did not stop students from protesting at any point in time, while at the same time, it was gearing up to conduct the NEET re-examination in time and punish the culprits who had engaged in paper leaks, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said."Permission was given when they came, as soon as Dipke landed. We didn't try at any point in time to stop the protest at all. When things didn't go right at the first time when the exams were held and leak became public, and it had to be acted upon, soon the govt arrested those who had bought and sold the papers. It was the responsibility of the govt to arrest them and put into the judicial process... but equally important was that the re-examination happens in time, so that one whole year does not get affected," Sitharaman said on why the govt took long to respond to the students' protest.She stressed it was after the successful re-examination that education minister Dharmendra Pradhan took the "wise" decision to resign. "If he hadn't done that (the re-examination process), it would have been irresponsible of everybody in the system," she said.Besides, she said, India faced the risk of inflation from both external and internal factors. "...this year, there is El Nino. The catchment areas are not receiving adequate rains. So, water for irrigation and drinking is going to pose a challenge. So, inflation cannot be just imported. It is also our own," she said.
Article Summary: Government did not stop students from protesting at any point in time, says nirmala sitharaman. At the same time, it was gearing up to conduct the neet re-examination in time and punish the culprits who had engaged in paper leaks, she says.

Article Title: Ship with 4 Indians hit at Ukraine port; 2 safe, fate of 2 unknown
Article Text:
File photo: A merchant vessel carrying four Indian nationals was struck at Ukraine's Port of Odesa

Government asks sailors for detailed info on ship’s intended route

NEW DELHI: Following the killing of five Indian nationals in the Russia-Ukraine conflict in recent days, the govt warned Indians intending to undertake employment on commercial vessels operating in or transiting the conflict-affected Black Sea region to carefully assess the prevailing security risks before accepting such assignments.The advisory came hours after a merchant vessel carrying four Indians was struck at Ukraine's Odesa port. India's embassy in Ukraine said on Sunday that while two of the Indians were safe, information about the other two was awaited.The incident occurred on Saturday when MV AGN Ragnar was hit at the port of Odesa, one of Ukraine's key Black Sea ports that has frequently come under attack since the outbreak of the Russia-Ukraine conflict. The embassy said search and rescue operations were in progress and that it was in constant contact with the authorities concerned to ascertain the status of the missing crew members and provide all possible assistance.The MEA advisory said those who choose to undertake such employment should exercise utmost caution.“The security situation in and around the Black Sea and adjoining maritime areas remains highly volatile due to the ongoing conflict.Commercial vessels operating in or transiting these waters are facing significant security risks, including missile and drone attacks,” said the ministry.It added that since April 2026, there has been an increase in the number of such incidents on commercial vessels resulting in the loss of five Indian lives.Govt also asked Indian nationals to obtain comprehensive information from employers/recruitment agencies and ship operators regarding the vessel’s intended route, ports of call, security arrangements, insurance coverage and emergency response procedures.Meanwhile, urging all stakeholders to be more cautious in the light of ongoing tension across sea routes, the country’s maritime regulator DG Shipping on Friday retweeted the advisory of Information Fusion Centre – Indian Ocean Region (IFCIOR), a 24x7 regional maritime security centre hosted by the Indian Navy.In the post on X, IFCIOR said maritime security environment across Strait of Hormuz, Gulf of Aden, Bab-al-Mandab and Red Sea remained “highly volatile”, with concurrent hybrid threats, piracy activity and route-specific risks affecting commercial shipping.
Article Summary: Government asks sailors for detailed info on ship’s intended route. Advisory came hours after a merchant vessel carrying four indians was struck at ukraine's odesa port. India's embassy in ukraine said on sunday that while two of the indians were safe, information about the other two was awaited.

Article Title: Sonam Wangchuk to be discharged from hospital on Monday after CJP ends 36-day protest
Article Text:
Sonam Wangchuk

Protest ends after Pradhan's resignation

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think of Sonam Wangchuk methods of activism? Inspiring and necessary Radical and unnecessary 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk will be discharged from Medanta Hospital in Gurugram on Monday after recovering from a 26-day indefinite fast in support of students protesting alleged irregularities in the NEET examination, his team said.Wangchuk is expected to be discharged at around 11.30 am. Before returning to his home in Ladakh, he will visit Rajghat to pay homage to Mahatma Gandhi. He had also paid tribute at Rajghat on June 28 before joining the agitation at Jantar Mantar.The activist joined the protest on June 28 and remained on an indefinite fast for 26 days. On July 18, he was shifted to Safdarjung Hospital, where he alleged that he was being kept in detention.Following an order of the Delhi high court, he was later transferred to Medanta Hospital for treatment.The 36-day agitation, led by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), concluded on Saturday after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister from the Union council of ministers. The protest, which began on June 20, demanded accountability over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations and reforms to the examination system.The CJP announced the withdrawal of its agitation in "good faith" after Pradhan stepped down and the organisation received assurances from the Centre on its other demands.Pradhan had said he submitted his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the interest of students and to ensure that the ongoing protests were not exploited by "anti-national forces." Following his resignation, President Droupadi Murmu assigned the additional charge of the Ministry of Education to Union minister Pralhad Joshi, who has since assumed office.
Article Summary: Sonam wangchuk will be discharged from medanta hospital in gurugram on monday. He had been on an indefinite fast in support of students protesting alleged irregularities in the neet examination. The 36-day agitation concluded on saturday after dharmendra pradhan resigned as education minister.

Article Title: ‘No law bars eating chicken over Ganga’: SC judge flags delayed bail at NLIU lecture
Article Text:
File photo: Justice Ujjwal Bhuyan

Bar and Bench

Raises concerns over delayed bail, restrictive conditions

Refers to Bombay HC order on Gaza protest

Calls for scrutiny of judicial decisions

Similar concerns raised earlier

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the courts impose less restrictive conditions when granting bail related to protests? Yes, it's necessary No, they should remain strict 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Saturday questioned the criminalisation of ordinary activities while highlighting delays in granting relief to citizens facing criminal action for protest or dissent, saying there is "no law prohibiting consumption of chicken over the Ganga river. "Speaking at the Justice GP Singh 4th Memorial Lecture at the National Law Institute University (NLIU) in Bhopal, Justice Bhuyan cited the arrest of 14 Muslim men who were accused of consuming chicken biryani while breaking their Ramzan fast on a boat in the Ganga as an example of what he described as the criminalisation of normal activities."Take for example the case of a group of youngsters breaking their fast over the river Ganga by consuming chicken biryani. I am sure consuming chicken biryani is not an offence. It can't be an offence. There is no law prohibiting consumption of chicken over the Ganga river. They were arrested for that very reason and they had to remain in jail for 3 months," he said, as quoted byJustice Bhuyan said such cases also highlighted broader concerns over how courts deal with petitions filed by citizens accused in protest-related cases.He observed that while courts often grant bail or other relief, it frequently comes after considerable delay and is accompanied by restrictive conditions.The judge said the space for expressing divergent opinions in India was shrinking and cautioned against the criminalisation of peaceful democratic activities."It will not be an exaggeration to say that public space for expressing divergent opinion is shrinking in India. The right to express one's views and to demonstrate peacefully are fundamental freedoms of the citizens. Debate and dissent are the essence of democracy. Unfortunately, even normal activities are being criminalised," he said.Justice Bhuyan also questioned the nature of conditions imposed while granting bail, suggesting that some restrictions could have a chilling effect on citizens exercising their right to dissent."These issues raise serious questions. Citizens are finding that though the courts are responsive and do grant bail, do grant relief, many a times it is belated. But it is the restrictive conditions which are imposed while granting bail that are causing the greatest concern. By such restrictive orders, are the courts indirectly telling the citizens or discouraging the citizens not to express their dissent?" he said.He also cited cases where courts granted bail but directed accused persons not to attend public meetings, post on social media or leave the country, saying such conditions could undermine fundamental freedoms.Justice Bhuyan also referred to a July 2025 Bombay high court order dismissing a petition filed by the Communist Party of India (Marxist), which had sought permission to hold a protest at Mumbai's Azad Maidan against the alleged genocide in Gaza.The high court had observed, "Our country has enough issues. We don't want anything like this. I am sorry to say, you are all short-sighted. You are looking at issues in Gaza and Palestine. Look at your own country. Be patriots. This is not patriotism. People say they are patriots."Commenting on the order, Justice Bhuyan said he found it "very amusing" that a judge questioned why citizens wished to protest over developments outside India.Justice Bhuyan said the judiciary is not above criticism and stressed that judgments should be critically examined by lawyers, students and the wider legal community."Judgments, after being delivered, are required to be critically examined and criticised if necessary. Criticism of a judgment does not amount to criticism of a judge."Referring to recent Supreme Court decisions, including the verdict on reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), he encouraged students to analyse judgments critically rather than accepting them unquestioningly."If everybody goes and tells the judges, 'Sir, wonderful thing. Sir, what you say is excellent. Sir, you are a jurist,' then how will the system improve?" he said.Justice Bhuyan also said judges should regularly introspect if they wish to retain public confidence in the institution."For the judges and the judiciary to remain legitimate and to remain relevant, public perception is most crucial... It is not for us to make that comment. It is for the citizens to assess. Perception of the citizens as to where the judiciary stands today, more particularly the Supreme Court, 75 years after we have become a Republic, is what matters," he said.He added that institutional improvement depends on introspection and that robust public debate, including criticism of judicial decisions, strengthens democratic institutions.Justice Bhuyan has previously voiced similar concerns about shrinking space for debate and dissent.Speaking at a Supreme Court Bar Association conference in Bengaluru earlier this year, he said a developed India would require greater tolerance for diverse views and cautioned against criminalising dissent.During that address, he also questioned the extensive use of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), pointing to low conviction rates and arguing that prolonged incarceration without timely trials could not be a model for a developed nation.
Article Summary: Supreme court judge justice ujjal bhuyan questioned the criminalisation of ordinary activities. He also highlighted delays in granting relief to citizens facing criminal action for protest or dissent. He cited the arrest of 14 muslim men who were accused of consuming chicken biryani while breaking their ramzan fast.

Article Title: 'Misrepresents statement': MEA fact-checks viral claim on spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal's remarks on CJP protests
Article Text:
MEA Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe the claims of foreign funding behind the CJP protests are justified? Yes, there is a basis for these claims No, the claims are unfounded 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Sunday termed as "misleading" a social media post claiming that ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal had said there was no foreign funding behind the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led youth protest in Delhi.The CJP stir, followed by demonstrations in other parts of the country, led to the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET (UG) question paper leak and other related issues."The post is misleading and misrepresents the statement of the spokesperson," the MEA's fact-check unit wrote on X, referring to the statement attributed to Jaiswal.It also shared Jaiswal's actual response to a query on allegations of foreign funding behind the CJP-led demonstrations."Madhu, regarding the point you raised about allegations of foreign funding and other such claims in connection with the ongoing protests, I would like to say that I do not have any information on this matter to share with you at this time," he replied during a weekly media briefing on Friday.The clarification came in response to a viral post on X claiming that Jaiswal had said, "I have been asked about the funding of the CJP protest many a time.I want to say that our intelligence & investigation reveals there is no foreign funding in it."CJP, an online satirical platform, was formed following a remark by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, in which he described a section of unemployed youth as "cockroaches." The CJI later clarified that he had been misquoted.The allegations of foreign funding have largely been linked to the fact that Abhijit Dipke, who founded the outfit, is a former student of Boston University. Dipke founded CJP in Boston and returned to India in June to lead its demonstrations seeking accountability over the NEET (UG) paper leak in May.The demonstrations peaked on July 20 with the group's "Chalo Sansad" march to Parliament, where protesters faced police action. The crackdown drew criticism from opposition parties, while the police maintained that the protest had turned violent.The 37-day-long agitation culminated in Pradhan's resignation on Saturday afternoon. The CJP called off its stir after the government accepted all its demands.Union minister Pralhad Joshi has been assigned additional charge of Pradhan's ministry of human resource development.
Article Summary: Mea calls as "misleading" a social media post claiming that ministry spokesperson randhir jaiswal had said there was no foreign funding behind the cockroach janta party (cjp)-led youth protest. Cjp stir, followed by demonstrations in other parts of the country, led to the resignation of union education minister dharmendra pradhan over the alleged neet (ug) question paper leak.

Article Title: 'This is a new subject for me': Pralhad Joshi after taking charge as education minister
Article Text:
Joshi thanks PM Modi, says he accepts responsibility with humility

Assigned additional charge after Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation

Poll Vote & Share your view What is the most pressing issue Joshi should address in education? Examination irregularities Improving quality of education Transparency in educational policies 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Change comes amid protests over examination irregularities

NEW DELHI: Union minister Pralhad Joshi on Sunday assumed charge as the Union education minister, a day after President Droupadi Murmu accepted the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan and assigned him the additional responsibility of the ministry. Taking charge, Joshi said he was reviewing the ministry's functioning and familiarising himself with the department, describing education as "a new subject" for him.Speaking to reporters after assuming office, Joshi said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had entrusted him with the responsibility and that he would take time to understand the ministry before making detailed comments."The Prime Minister has entrusted me with this responsibility with full confidence.I was in Karnataka yesterday. I reached here last night and came this morning to take charge. I have assumed charge. I am reviewing all the details here and the decisions that need to be taken. I have been gathering information and trying to understand the functioning of the entire ministry. We had continuous meetings today. This is a new subject for me. I have taken charge today and held detailed discussions with the senior officers.It is a very big department, so I will speak to you in detail after I have understood it completely," Joshi said.Soon after taking charge, Joshi shared a message on X thanking Prime Minister Narendra Modi for entrusting him with the Education Ministry."Today, I assumed charge as the Union Minister for Education. I am grateful to Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi ji for placing his faith in me and entrusting me with this responsibility," he wrote.He added, "I accept it with humility and a deep sense of duty."Joshi was given charge of the Education ministry on Saturday after President Droupadi Murmu accepted Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation from the Union council of ministers with immediate effect.According to a Rashtrapati Bhavan statement, Joshi will continue to hold his existing portfolios while also heading the Education Ministry."The President of India, as advised by the Prime Minister, has accepted the resignation of Shri Dharmendra Pradhan from the Union Council of Ministers, with immediate effect, under clause (2) of Article 75 of the Constitution of India. Further, as advised by the Prime Minister, the President has directed that Shri Pralhad Joshi, Cabinet Minister, be assigned the charge of the Ministry of Education, in addition to his existing portfolio," the statement said.Joshi is currently the Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution and New and Renewable Energy. He has previously served as the Union Minister for Coal, Mines and Parliamentary Affairs.The change at the top of the education ministry comes after weeks of nationwide student protests over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations, including the NEET paper leak. Students have been demanding greater transparency, accountability and reforms in the examination system.Dharmendra Pradhan announced his resignation on Saturday, saying he had submitted it to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the interest of students and to ensure that the ongoing protests over examination irregularities were not exploited by "anti-national forces."Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) announced that it had withdrawn its 36-day-long agitation at Jantar Mantar in "good faith" after Pradhan stepped down from the Union council of ministers and the organisation received assurances from the government on its other demands.
Article Summary: Joshi thanks pm modi, says he accepts responsibility with humility and a deep sense of duty. President droupadi murmu accepted the resignation of dharmendra pradhan and assigned him the additional responsibility of the ministry. Joshi is currently the union minister for consumer affairs, food and public distribution and new and renewable energy.

Article Title: 'PM Modi's apology awaited': Opposition to keep up NEET protest pressure in Parliament
Article Text:
File photo: Opposition & ruling party MPs staged counter-protests & raised slogans against each other outside Parliament on Thursday (Picture credit: PTI)

Rahul Gandhi seeks answers from Amit Shah

Opposition to decide stand on anti-paper leak bill

NEW DELHI: The Congress-led opposition is set to keep up the pressure on the government in Parliament over the alleged police brutality against students protesting the NEET-UG paper leak, with demands for action against those responsible for the assault and an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, sources quoted by news agency PTI said on Sunday.The opposition's floor strategy, including its stand on the proposed amendment to the anti-paper leak law, will be finalised at a meeting of INDIA bloc leaders in Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge's chamber on Monday morning, the sources said.The developments come ahead of what is expected to be a heated debate in Parliament over the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, which has been listed for introduction, consideration and passage in the Lok Sabha on Monday.Ahead of the Parliament session, leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi wrote to Union home minister Amit Shah, demanding accountability for what he described as the "barbaric assault" on peacefully protesting students and questioning whether the home minister had authorised the use of "lethal force", including pellet guns.In the letter, the Congress MP said peaceful protest is a cornerstone of democracy and it is the government's responsibility to protect protesters and address their grievances through dialogue."Such brutal violence destroys every norm, and has outraged the country. Youth and students, the future of our country, are demanding answers and accountability. Their voice will be heard," he wrote.Sharing the letter on X, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said Gandhi had asked Shah two questions: "As the Home Minister, did you authorise the use of lethal force, including pellet guns, against students? If not, who granted this authorisation? Are the individuals seen raining blows on students while dressed in plain clothes, police personnel or volunteers? Who authorised their deployment?""The home minister must answer these crucial questions in Parliament tomorrow. The prime minister should apologise to the students," Ramesh added.Rahul had earlier alleged that security personnel used pellet guns, tear gas and batons against peaceful protesters during the July 20 march to Parliament.He also referred to 19-year-old student Sahil Lochab, claiming the youth could lose an eye after allegedly being struck by pellets. Delhi Police has denied using pellet guns during the protest, while the CRPF has not responded to the allegation.The Congress has described education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as a victory for students but has maintained that Prime Minister Modi should also apologise over the alleged police action.Kharge has said it is now the prime minister's turn to apologise and take strict action against those responsible for using lathis, batons and pellet guns against protesting students.After Pradhan's resignation, Rahul also urged PM Modi to apologise to students "out of respect for the future of the country" and for the alleged "atrocities" committed during the protests."This is not the end. We still await the prime minister's apology to our students," Ramesh said, reiterating the demand for accountability for those responsible for the alleged excesses.A heated debate on the paper leak issue is likely if the government and opposition can resolve the ongoing deadlock in both Houses of Parliament.The opposition will also decide whether to support the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026.The proposed legislation seeks to tighten punishments for examination-related offences. Individuals involved in paper leaks or other unfair means would face imprisonment ranging from five to 10 years and fines of up to Rs 50 lakh. Organised crimes related to examination fraud would attract a minimum seven-year jail term and fines of up to Rs 10 crore.The existing law prescribes imprisonment of three to five years for cheating-related offences, while organised exam fraud currently attracts five to 10 years in prison and a minimum fine of Rs 1 crore.Asked on Saturday whether the Congress would support the new bill, Rahul said the party would take a decision only after consultations with other opposition parties."The Congress party has a central principle. We will decide this during a meeting of opposition parties and a decision will be based on opposition consensus. In Parliament, that is our discipline, and that is our way of functioning," he said.The government announced the proposed amendments after student protests over the NEET-UG paper leak intensified across the country. Prime Minister Modi has also promised fast-track courts and stricter punishment for those involved in paper leak cases.The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which spearheaded the agitation, called off its 36-day protest on Saturday after the resignation of the education minister and the government's acceptance of its other demands.
Article Summary: Opposition to decide stand on anti-paper leak bill on monday, sources say. Rahul gandhi writes to amit shah demanding accountability for 'barbaric assault' on students. Opposition will also decide whether to support the public examinations (prevention of unfair means) amendment bill.

Article Title: 'Beginning of accountability': Prashant Kishor on Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
Article Text:
Prashant Kishor said the movement had gone beyond political affiliations.

NEW DELHI: Jan Suraaj founder and Bankipur assembly by-election candidate Prashant Kishor on Sunday described Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as the "beginning of accountability", asserting that sustained public pressure had compelled the government to act.Addressing reporters, Kishor said the movement had gone beyond political affiliations and demonstrated that public mobilisation could force those in power to respond."This is the beginning of accountability. Accountability is being enforced under public pressure. I always say that in this country, the opposition party can be weak. The opposition cannot be weak," he said.Expressing support for those opposing what he termed the government's "undemocratic behaviour", Kishor said the issue was larger than any single political party."We stand with anyone who wants to challenge this government's undemocratic behaviour and their work. Sonam Wangchuk is my friend. He's a prominent academic, environmentalist, and friend of ours. This isn't about a party; people have seen that if people stand up, if the public rises, even those in power will have to bow down," he said.Referring to the ongoing protests in Delhi, Kishor said they reflected widespread public anger rather than the agenda of any one organisation."What you and I are seeing in Delhi wasn't a protest by one Sonam Wangchuk. The thousands of people who came to protest didn't carry CJP flags. They were ordinary young people, frustrated by the daily paper leaks, unemployment, and the crumbling education system," he said.Commenting on the arrest of Janshakti Janata Dal national president Tej Pratap Yadav, Kishor alleged that the action reflected the government's nervousness."Tej Pratap announced his support yesterday, and at 1.30 am last night, Tej Pratap was arrested and sent to Beur Jail. This shows how scared these people are. Under what section was he arrested? Why was he arrested? The police administration should explain this," he was quoted as saying by news agency ANI.Kishor claimed Pradhan's resignation was only the beginning and suggested that the agitation would continue."Dharmendra Pradhan had to leave, and that's not all, this is just the beginning. This isn't going to stop," he added.Kishor also raised objections to an order issued by the district magistrate regarding election awareness activities involving Jeevika Didis. He urged the election commission and its observers to take note of the matter and initiate action."The District Magistrate issued order. In which he stated that Jeevika Didi, would work for election awareness. We hope that the Election Commission, their observers, will take cognizance of this matter, and take action," he said.He warned that if no action was taken by Monday, he and his supporters would stage a protest outside the Election Commission's office."If action isn't taken by tomorrow, we will go to the Election Commission and sit on a protest at their gate, along with my colleagues," Kishor said.
Article Summary: Jan suraaj founder and bankipur assembly by-election candidate prashant kishor described union education minister dharmendra pradhan's resignation as the "beginning of accountability" he said the movement had gone beyond political affiliations and demonstrated that public mobilisation could force those in power to respond.

Article Title: India issues Black Sea advisory after strike in Ukraine's Odesa, calls maritime corridor 'highly volatile'
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs has issued a fresh advisory urging Indian nationals to exercise extreme caution before accepting employment on commercial vessels operating in or transiting the Black Sea region.The ministry warned that the security situation in the conflict-hit maritime corridor remains "highly volatile", with commercial vessels facing persistent risks from missile and drone attacks.This comes after a merchant vessel carrying four Indian nationals was struck at Ukraine's Port of Odesa, with two crew members confirmed safe while the status of the other two is still being ascertained, according to the Indian Embassy in Kyiv.In an advisory issued on Sunday, New Delhi said that the deteriorating security environment has already claimed the lives of five Indian nationals since April 2026."The security situation in and around the Black Sea and adjoining maritime areas remains highly volatile due to the ongoing conflict. Commercial vessels operating in or transiting these waters are facing significant security risks, including missile and drone attacks," the Ministry of External Affairs said.The advisory follows a string of attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea amid the Russia-Ukraine war. On July 18, an Indian seafarer was killed after the merchant vessel MV Omorfi was attacked while transiting the Black Sea, marking the second attack on a ship carrying Indian crew within a week and taking the total number of Indian seafarers killed in the conflict to five. New Delhi had earlier condemned attacks on merchant shipping and called for safe maritime navigation.Advising seafarers to carefully assess the risks before accepting assignments in the region, the ministry urged them to verify vessel routes, security arrangements, insurance cover, emergency procedures and employment terms.It also said Indian nationals should "ensure that the terms of employment comply with applicable international maritime standards and provide adequate provisions for medical care, evacuation, repatriation, and compensation in the event of an emergency."The ministry also stressed the importance of maintaining communication with family members during voyages. "Keep family members informed of your itinerary and maintain regular contact," it said.It also directed Indian nationals to closely follow safety guidance issued by the Directorate General of Maritime Administration, other Government of India authorities, vessel operators and competent maritime authorities."Regularly monitor and comply with advisories issued by the Directorate General of Maritime Administration, and other relevant Government of India authorities, as well as safety instructions issued by vessel operators and the competent maritime authorities," the ministry said.The advisory added that Indian nationals requiring assistance should remain in touch with India's Embassy and Consulates in the region through the emergency contact numbers provided in the advisory.
Article Summary: The security situation in the conflict-hit maritime corridor remains "highly volatile" commercial vessels facing persistent risks from missile and drone attacks. The advisory follows a string of attacks on commercial vessels in the black sea amid the russia-ukraine war.

Article Title: Pralhad Joshi takes charge as Union education minister a day after Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
Article Text:
Pralhad Joshi takes charge as Union education minister

NEW DELHI: Pralhad Joshi on Sunday took charge as Union education minister. This came a day after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned from the role amid student protests at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi and nationwide.Earlier, Pradhan shared his resignation letter on X, addressing it to his "young friends". He said he had submitted his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in view of the situation that had unfolded across the country.The CJP-led protest was later called off after a delegation of the group held talks with Union ministers Jagat Prakash Nadda and Jitendra Singh, with both sides reaching a mutual understanding on the protesters' key demands.Born on November 27, 1962, in Bijapur, Karnataka, Pralhad Joshi completed his schooling in Hubballi. He attended Railway School for his primary education and later studied at New English School before graduating with a bachelor's degree in arts from Shri Kadasiddheshwar Arts College, Hubballi.Before joining politics full-time, Joshi was associated with business. He later emerged as a prominent Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader in Karnataka and has represented the Dharwad Lok Sabha constituency since 2004, winning five consecutive terms in Parliament.Over the years, Joshi has held several key organisational and ministerial positions. Between 2019 and 2024, he served as the Union Minister for Parliamentary Affairs, Coal and Mines. Following the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, he was entrusted with the portfolios of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and New and Renewable Energy.As Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy, Joshi has overseen several flagship government initiatives, including the National Green Hydrogen Mission, PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, PM-KUSUM, and programmes aimed at expanding India's renewable energy capacity.

Article Title: 'Every misadventure by Pakistan will draw response beyond their imagination': Rajnath Singh on Vijay Diwas

'Army fully prepared'

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Sunday issued a stern warning to Pakistan, saying every "misadventure" would invite a response "beyond their imagination".While addressing the nation on the 27th Kargil Vijay Diwas at the Kargil War Memorial in Drass, Ladakh, he said, ""Our intention is clear. There will be no talks with Pakistan. If there are any talks, they will be only on PoK, which is a part of India and illegally occupied by Pakistan. ""At present, Pakistan has made terrorism a part of its government policy, and the distinction between the military and militants has completely disappeared there. The army not only protects terrorist organizations but also works closely with them. Therefore, during Operation Sindoor, we made it clear that India will no longer view terrorists and the governments that support them separately," he added.Drawing a sharp contrast between India and Pakistan, Defence minister Rajnath Singh further said that India is focused on innovation, technology and development, while Pakistan continues to promote infiltration and terrorism."India is pursuing innovation, while Pakistan is seeking new ways of infiltration. While India is designing ships, Pakistan is engaged in designing terrorism," he said.In his address while reiterating India's firm stand on Pakistan, Rajnath Singh said there would be no talks with Islamabad, except on Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), which he described as an integral part of India under illegal occupation."Our intention is clear. There will be no talks with Pakistan. If there are any talks, they will be only on PoK, which is a part of India and illegally occupied by Pakistan."In an X post on Sunday, Singh wrote, "On the occasion of Kargil Vijay Diwas, I pay my deepest respects to all the brave soldiers who laid down their lives in the defense of our motherland. The nation will forever remain grateful and indebted to all those valiant soldiers who demonstrated extraordinary valor on the inaccessible peaks of Kargil in 1999."He added that the Indian Army 's indomitable courage, sacrifice and unwavering resolve would continue to inspire future generations with patriotism, dedication to duty and "the spirit of offering everything for the motherland."Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday asserted that the Indian Army is "fully prepared" to tackle any challenge, saying the "intent of infiltrators" has remained unchanged since the 1999 Kargil conflict.Speaking to Army personnel at a Shaurya Bhoj in Dras on Kargil Vijay Diwas, after attending Shaurya Sandhya at the Kargil War Memorial, Singh paid tribute to the soldiers who laid down their lives during the 1999 war and said that while India celebrates their sacrifice, the country must remain vigilant against continuing threats such as proxy war and cross-border infiltration."We have to remember that even today challenges have not reduced; the intent of infiltrators hasn't changed, and even today it adopts tools like a proxy war or infiltration," Singh said, in an apparent reference to Pakistan."I am fully assured that our Army is fully prepared for any such challenges," he added.Observed every year on July 26, Kargil Vijay Diwas commemorates India's victory in the 1999 Kargil War, honours the 527 soldiers who laid down their lives during Operation Vijay and pays tribute to the courage of thousands who fought in one of the world's toughest battlefields.
Article Summary: Defence minister rajnath singh issues stern warning to pakistan. He says every "misadventure" would invite a response "beyond their imagination" singh: india is focused on innovation, technology and development, while pakistan continues to promote infiltration and terrorism.

Article Title: Nepal eases rules on Indian currency, allows Rs 200 and Rs 500 notes up to Rs 25,000
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Nepal has eased restrictions on the movement of Indian currency, allowing Indian and Nepali citizens to carry Indian Rs 200 and Rs 500 notes issued after November 9, 2016. According to the Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB), the permitted notes can be carried into or taken out of Nepal up to a limit of Rs 25,000 per person.According to news agency PTI, the revised rules permit citizens of both countries to bring the approved currency notes into Nepal, carry them within the country, or take them out, subject to existing regulations.In its latest notice, the NRB clarified that older Indian currency notes issued before the 2016 demonetisation period will continue to remain prohibited in Nepal.The NRB added that only redesigned Indian Rs 500 notes and Rs 200 notes introduced after November 9, 2016, will be permitted under the new arrangement.The central bank had initially published the provision in the Nepal Gazette on February 11. However, it issued another notice on Thursday to clarify the implementation process and address concerns over cross-border currency movement.NRB spokesperson Guru Prasad Paudel said Nepali citizens would not be allowed to bring Indian currency into Nepal from countries other than India.He also clarified that Indian currency taken out of Nepal by Nepali citizens could only be carried to India and not to any third country.The new provision would facilitate Indian tourists visiting Nepal and Nepalese nationals engaged in trade and business with India, said Paudel.The rule change comes after years of restrictions introduced following India’s demonetisation announcement on November 8, 2016, when the old Rs 500 and Rs 1,000 notes were withdrawn from circulation.Following the move, Nepal had restricted the use and movement of those discontinued Indian notes due to concerns over their circulation and financial impact.The latest decision affects cross-border transactions between India and Nepal, which share an open border and extensive economic links. India remains Nepal’s largest trading partner and a key source of tourists, while thousands of Nepali citizens travel to India for work, education and business.The NRB also stated that Nepali citizens and foreign visitors can bring foreign currency worth up to $5,000, or its equivalent in other currencies, into Nepal without filing a customs declaration. Amounts above that threshold must be declared upon arrival.
Article Summary: Nepal has eased restrictions on the movement of indian currency. Indian and nepali citizens can carry indian rs 200 and rs 500 notes issued after november 9, 2016. The permitted notes can be carried into or taken out of nepal up to a limit of rs 25,000.

Article Title: 'Gratitude to brave soldiers': PM Modi pays tribute to Kargil heroes on 27th Vijay Diwas
Article Text:
India is observing the 27th anniversary of Kargil Vijay Diwas.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday paid tribute to the soldiers of the Indian Armed Forces on the occasion of the 27th Kargil Vijay Diwas and remembered their role in safeguarding the country's sovereignty."On Kargil Vijay Diwas, our nation expresses gratitude to the brave soldiers for their extraordinary courage and commitment towards securing India. Their valour in the face of the most formidable conditions will forever remain a source of national pride. Their unwavering patriotism and devotion to duty will continue to inspire generations," the Prime Minister said in a post on X.India is observing the 27th anniversary of Kargil Vijay Diwas, commemorating its victory in the 1999 Kargil War. The day marks the successful culmination of Operation Vijay and honours the 527 soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice while driving Pakistani intruders out of strategic heights in the Kargil sector.The Kargil conflict, fought between May and July 1999, remains the only conventional war between two nuclear-armed neighbours. The battles were fought across the rugged mountain terrain of Kargil, Dras, Batalik, Mushkoh and Kaksar in Ladakh at altitudes exceeding 5,000 metres.Despite freezing temperatures, low oxygen levels and heavily fortified enemy positions, Indian troops recaptured the occupied peaks without crossing the Line of Control, earning global recognition for their professionalism and military restraint.Over the years, Kargil Vijay Diwas has come to symbolise not only India's military victory but also a defining moment that reshaped the country's defence preparedness, strategic planning and national security framework.Union home minister Amit Shah also paid tribute to the soldiers, describing Kargil Vijay Diwas as a symbol of the Indian Army's indomitable courage and extraordinary valour."'Kargil Vijay Diwas' stands as a symbol of the Indian Army's indomitable courage and extraordinary valour. In 1999, despite facing adverse conditions and enemy positions situated at high altitudes amidst the treacherous, snow-capped peaks of the Himalayas, our brave soldiers forced the enemy to their knees through 'Operation Vijay'. On 'Kargil Vijay Diwas', I pay tribute to all those brave sons who made the ultimate sacrifice to uphold the nation's integrity," Shah said.Defence minister Rajnath Singh , who attended the Kargil Vijay Diwas commemorations at the Kargil War Memorial in Dras on Saturday, said the intent of infiltrators had not changed since the 1999 conflict and asserted that the Indian Army remained fully prepared to counter any challenge."We have to remember that even today challenges have not reduced; the intent of infiltrators hasn't changed, and even today it adopts tools like a proxy war or infiltration," Singh said in an apparent reference to Pakistan."I am fully assured that our Army is fully prepared for any such challenges," he added.The defence minister also highlighted the government's focus on modernising the armed forces, saying sustained efforts were being made to equip the military with the latest technology and the best training. Referring to the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative, he expressed confidence that the Indian armed forces would emerge among the finest in the world.Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi also remembered the fallen soldiers, saying the nation would forever remain indebted to their courage, valour and supreme sacrifice."A humble tribute to all the brave soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice while defending India's borders, on Kargil Victory Day. The nation will forever remain indebted to your courage, valor, and supreme sacrifice," Gandhi wrote on X.
Article Summary: India is observing the 27th anniversary of kargil vijay diwas. The day marks the successful culmination of operation vijay. 527 soldiers made the supreme sacrifice while driving pakistani intruders out of strategic heights in the kargil sector.

Article Title: 'Don't insult students' intelligence': Rahul Gandhi slams PM Modi's midnight video on paper leaks

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi early Friday attacked Prime Minister Narendra Modi accusing him of sidestepping the demand for Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan 's resignation over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak.Reacting to the Prime Minister's late-night video message on the issue, Rahul said PM Modi should not "insult the intelligence" of students and demanded Pradhan be sacked saying the PM's address failed to raise students' key concerns.In a post on X, Rahul wrote, "Mr Modi, our students are demanding Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. Don't insult their intelligence with this pathetic midnight video."Listing his demands, he said:"1. Sack Pradhan.2. Punish those who beat students.3. Apologise."The leader of oppostion's remarks came hours after Prime Minister Modi announced that the government would bring a Bill in Parliament next week providing for stringent punishment against those involved in examination paper leaks.In a self-recorded video shared on X late Thursday night, the Prime Minister said the proposed legislation, which includes provisions for Fast-Track Courts and stricter penalties, would be discussed by the Union Cabinet on Friday before being introduced in Parliament when the second week of the Monsoon Session begins on Monday."Friends, I know that paper leaks are not an ordinary matter. For lakhs of students and their parents, it is extremely painful," PM Modi said."Our most important responsibility was to ensure that a whole year for the students is not wasted. It was very important to conduct the exams immediately. The government used its full strength to arrange exams for nearly 22 lakh students in the shortest possible time. And just five or six days ago, on the 19th, the results were also announced," he said.The Prime Minister said the government was now moving towards stronger legal action."Today I have issued directions to the departments to set up Fast-Track Courts. The departments worked tirelessly and, late last night, provided me with a draft. This draft, which includes provisions for Fast-Track Courts and stringent punishments, will be discussed in the Cabinet tomorrow," he said.He added that after incorporating suggestions from Cabinet colleagues, the Bill would be finalised and introduced in Parliament next week."Nothing is more important than the welfare and future of our youth. Those who try to harm the future of our youth will not be spared," PM Modi said.The opposition has been demanding Pradhan's resignation and a detailed discussion on the alleged NEET-UG paper leak during the Monsoon Session, with the issue triggering protests both inside Parliament and on the streets.Activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike on Friday at Medanta Hospital in the presence of Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh, along with senior leaders of the Apex Body of Leh.In a post on X, Wangchuk said he decided to end the fast after prolonged discussions and in view of the possibility of violence."Just now in the presence of Union Ministers JP Nadda & Dr. Jitendra Singh and the senior leaders of Apex Body of Leh Ladakh I finally broke my fast after 26 days... This was done after a long negotiation on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country," he said."I will explain the conditions in detail in a separate video very soon. Meanwhile urge you all to stay very vigilant about not allowing violence of any kind anywhere," he added.Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has called for nationwide peaceful protests on Friday, reiterating its demand for Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the alleged examination irregularities.
Article Summary: Rahul gandhi accuses prime minister narendra modi of sidestepping the demand for union education minister dharmendra pradhan's resignation over the alleged neet-ug 2026 paper leak. The leader of oppostion's remarks came hours after pm modi announced that the government would bring a bill in parliament next week providing for stringent punishment.
